question: Should this protected core-scheduler refactor merge after a current-head runtime cron lifecycle proof is added and the remaining checks finish?
rationale: The patch changes no stated product contract, but it reorganizes lifecycle and run-admission logic in a protected maintainer-reviewed area; test and CI output alone do not establish the requested after-fix real behavior proof.

options.title: Request runtime cron proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted current-head run covering scheduler start, a persisted job execution, and completion or reload confirmation before approving the refactor.

options.title: Accept existing automated coverage
options.body: A maintainer may accept the focused tests and changed gate as sufficient for this behavior-neutral internal refactor, explicitly owning the lack of direct runtime evidence.

recommendation.title: Request runtime cron proof
recommendation.body: Ask for a redacted current-head run covering scheduler start, a persisted job execution, and completion or reload confirmation before approving the refactor.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current cron split and follow-up correction, making them the best available routing candidate for the requested proof and design context.
